readout_other: wire hanging test, open field test, forced swimming test
direction_notes: TUS improved wire-hanging, open-field, and forced-swimming behavioral scores in the PD+TUS group relative to PD+Sham from day 4 onward, with no direct neurophysiological measure of excitation/inhibition reported.
safety_notes: Authors estimated the maximum temperature rise from ultrasound to be far below the threshold for thermal bioeffects, based on the maximum intensity and pulse duration used.

target.label: brain tissue without motor cortex; the subthalamic nucleus (STN) is one of nuclei in brain tissue covered by the ultrasound spot

timing.protocol_description: The interstimulus interval was 1 s, and the total stimulation time was 5 minutes for each stimulus. TUS was performed in the PD mice daily for 2 weeks.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The mice were divided randomly into four groups: healthy $( \mathrm { N } = 6 )$ , PD (N 8), PD Sham (N 8) and PD TUS $( \Nu = 8 )$ .
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: The TUS was performed in the PD mice daily for 2 weeks.
source_quotes.randomised: The mice were divided randomly into four groups: healthy $( \mathrm { N } = 6 )$ , PD (N 8), PD Sham (N 8) and PD TUS $( \Nu = 8 )$ .

flags.reason: Exact stimulation target is not given with stereotaxic coordinates; paper only states brain tissue excluding motor cortex, with STN noted as one nucleus covered by the ultrasound spot.
Paper does not state whether the measured pressure/intensity was measured in free field/water or in situ; hydrophone measurement setup relative to the animal is not specified.
Paper gives a separate 'stimulation duration (SD)' of 50 ms and a PRF/duty cycle but never states a distinct pulse duration; not computed per protocol (would be 0.05 ms from duty/PRF).
Only behavioral outcomes were assessed; no neurophysiological measure of excitatory/inhibitory direction was reported.
